S84.01.note: The drop-down's accessible name is Display language (LanguageSelector.tsx); how Settings is opened from the first screen was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and choose General in the settings list (the group is titled Settings).
Find the row labelled Display Language and open its drop-down (options show a flag and the language's own name).
Pick a different language.
Look at whether the interface text switches to that language, and compare with Expected.

S84.03.note: packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts labels the same appearance key Personalization, while web-settings-navigation.ts labels it Appearance; the tester should use the label on screen.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Theme with three buttons: System, Light, Dark.
Click Light, then Dark, then System.
Look whether the colours of the whole app change each time and whether the choice is still selected after closing and reopening Settings.

S84.04.note: The accent row is rendered without a visible condition in this file; whether it is hidden on some plans or surfaces was not checked.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Accent colour and its group of colour buttons.
Click a different accent colour.
Look whether buttons, links and highlights across the app take the new colour.

S84.05.note: Options are Small, Default and Large.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Chat text size and open its drop-down.
Choose Large, then Small.
Open a chat with several messages and look whether message text grows and shrinks.

S84.07.note: System follows the operating-system preference; the exact OS setting was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Motion with two buttons: System and Reduced.
Click Reduced.
Trigger an animation in chat (for example send a message or open a menu) and look whether motion is reduced; then check that System follows the device reduce-motion setting.

S84.08.needs: a chat that shows a code block
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Code theme and open its drop-down.
Pick a different code theme.
Open a chat that shows a code block and look whether its colours change.

S84.09.needs: a chat with a long line of code
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Find the row labelled Wrap long code lines and turn its switch on or off.
Open a chat with a code block that has a very long line.
Look whether the long line wraps onto the next line or runs off to the side.
S84.09.where: Settings > Appearance > Wrap long code lines

S84.10.needs: none; a model marked Upgrade to use needs a paid plan to choose
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled Default model and open its drop-down; the first option is Last used.
Pick a model name (a model marked Upgrade to use is locked to your plan).
Open a new chat and look whether the model picker starts on the chosen model.
Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled Reasoning effort and open its drop-down.
Choose a different effort level (levels above your plan are marked and cannot be picked).
Open a new chat and look whether the effort picker in the composer shows the chosen level.

S84.12.needs: a paid plan may be needed for Work (the row shows a plan hint)
S84.12.note: The row shows a plan-entitlement hint from planCapabilityEntitlementHint; the exact gating was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and choose General.
Find the row labelled New chats start in and open its drop-down (options Chat and Work).
Choose Work.
Click the new-chat control and look whether the new chat opens in Work mode.
S84.12.where: Settings > General > New chats start in

S84.14.note: This is an on/off switch only; the code does not offer a choice of which modifier sends, unlike Expected's wording.
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then scroll to the heading Composer.
Turn the switch on the row labelled Send with Enter on or off.
Read the hint under the row (it says Off: Enter starts a new line and the key combination sends).
Open a chat, type two lines, press Enter, and look whether the message sends or a new line is added.
S84.14.where: Settings > General > Composer > Send with Enter

S84.15.note: The shortcut pane is KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx; the desktop shortcut settings (Quick Ask and others) are listed under S84.22 and the Desktop app group.
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then find the row labelled Keyboard shortcuts and click View shortcuts (or choose the Keyboard item in the settings list).
Read the list of shortcuts and search with the field labelled Search shortcuts.
Click the control labelled Change keys for a rebindable shortcut and press a new key combination.
Turn off a shortcut with its on/off switch and look whether the list updates and the key stops working.
S84.15.where: Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts > View shortcuts, or Settings > Keyboard

S84.18.needs: a second device or email inbox to confirm delivery; mobile push needs the phone app
S84.18.note: Channel names are Browser, Email, Mobile push and Push (per event); the exact menu for picking channels was not fully traced.
steps: Open Settings and choose Notifications.
Find the event rows (for example Reply ready, Scheduled task finished, Security alerts) and open the choice for each.
Choose a channel combination (Browser, Email, Mobile push, or Push where shown) or Off.
Trigger or wait for that event and look whether it arrives on the chosen channel only.

S84.19.note: Whether notifications are actually held during the window needs a real notification to check; that was not traced.
steps: Open Settings and choose Time and focus.
Find the row labelled Quiet hours and turn on its switch labelled Enable quiet hours.
Set the start and end time using the fields labelled Quiet hours start and Quiet hours end.
Read the note under the row (it says notifications are held, and approvals and failures still arrive) and compare with Expected.
S84.19.where: Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours

S84.21.needs: the Electron desktop app on a Mac
S84.21.note: The desktop settings row is shown only when the app runs in the desktop host; the Launch at login label in apps/desktop/src is the internal Tauri build and is not the public app.
steps: In the desktop app, open Settings and choose General under the group Desktop app.
Find the row labelled Run on startup and turn its switch on.
Optionally open the Mac app menu (the app name menu) and look for the item Launch at Login, which should show a tick.
Quit and reopen the Mac, or log out and back in, and look whether AGI opens by itself.
S84.21.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Run on startup (desktop app only)

S84.22.needs: the Electron desktop app on a Mac
S84.22.note: The window's position on screen was not traced; the hint says it is for messaging AGI from anywhere on the desktop.
steps: In the desktop app, open Settings, choose General under Desktop app, and find the row labelled Quick Ask shortcut.
Open its drop-down (it lists shortcut choices, and No shortcut) and pick a different key combination or No shortcut.
Press the chosen combination from another app and look whether the Quick Ask window appears.
Open the Mac app menu or File menu and look for the item Quick Ask to compare the shortcut shown.
S84.22.where: Settings > Desktop app > General > Quick Ask shortcut (desktop app only)

labels.text: Hide anything you do not use from the left rail.

S84.23.note: Only the Sidebar items toggles were found; no collapsed-by-default or auto-hide setting exists in the settings files. Chat cannot be hidden. Sidebar collapse is a toggle in WebChatPage.tsx, not a setting.
steps: Open Settings and choose General, then find the row labelled Sidebar items.
Click a destination name (the hint says Hide anything you do not use from the left rail) to switch it off; click again to switch it on.
Close Settings and look at the left rail; the switched-off item should disappear and reappear when switched back on.
Check whether there is any control for collapsed-by-default or auto-hide (none was found).
